biological.citation: Activation of PDE2A moderates pathologically high cAMP/PKA responses to dopamine in dyskinetic mice (PMID: 40412662)
biological.summary: PDE2A is activated by cGMP signaling and efficiently reduces excessive cAMP/PKA signaling triggered by D1 receptor stimulation in striatal neurons of 6-OHDA Parkinson's disease mice. This regulatory effect occurs despite unaltered PDE2A expression, suggesting PDE2A activity modulation as a therapeutic target for L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia.

biological.citation: Phosphodiesterases PDE2A and PDE10A both change mRNA expression in the human brain with age, but only PDE2A changes in a region-specific manner with psychiatric disease (PMID: 32119913)
biological.summary: PDE2A mRNA expression is reduced in the amygdala of patients with schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, and bipolar disorder compared to controls. PDE2A expression changes in a disorder- and brain region-specific manner in frontal cortex (SCZ), caudal entorhinal cortex/hippocampus/striatum (BPD), with highest expression in cortex, hippocampus, and striatum.
biological.sample_size: Stanley Foundation Neuropathology Consortium postmortem brain samples

biological.citation: Towards selective phosphodiesterase 2A (PDE2A) inhibitors: a patent review (2010 - present) (PMID: 27321640)
biological.summary: PDE2A is a dual substrate enzyme that hydrolyzes both cAMP and cGMP. It is highly expressed in the brain, particularly in cortex, hippocampus, and striatum, where it regulates intraneuronal cGMP and cAMP levels in brain areas involved in emotion, perception, concentration, learning and memory.

biological.citation: CRISPR/Cas9 Knock-Out in Primary Neonatal and Adult Cardiomyocytes Reveals Distinct cAMP Dynamics Regulation by Various PDE2A and PDE3A Isoforms (PMID: 37296663)
biological.summary: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of PDE2A in primary rat cardiomyocytes achieved >50-60% protein reduction in neonatal cells and >95% in adult cells. Neonatal myocytes express only PDE2A2 isoform, while adult cardiomyocytes express all three isoforms (A1, A2, A3), each contributing distinctly to cAMP dynamics regulation.
biological.sample_size: Primary neonatal and adult rat ventricular cardiomyocytes

biological.citation: miR-139/PDE2A-Notch1 feedback circuit represses stemness of gliomas by inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin signaling (PMID: 34512162)
biological.summary: PDE2A suppresses Wnt/β-catenin signaling by inhibiting cAMP accumulation and GSK-3β phosphorylation, thereby modulating self-renewal of glioma stem cells. PDE2A is transcribed together with miR-139 from the same locus, and both are inversely correlated with glioma stem cell stemness and associated with better prognosis.
biological.sample_size: Patient-derived glioma stem-like cells and orthotopic xenografts

biological.citation: Gene therapy with phosphodiesterases 2A and 4B ameliorates heart failure and arrhythmias by improving subcellular cAMP compartmentation (PMID: 38776406)
biological.summary: PDE2A3 overexpression in cardiomyocytes restores altered cAMP compartmentation in caveolin-rich plasma membrane microdomains and ameliorates caveolin-3 decline. PDE2A gene therapy attenuates cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, and contractile dysfunction in pressure-overload heart failure mice.
biological.sample_size: Transverse aortic constriction mouse model with 8-week follow-up

biological.citation: Differential expression of the cyclic GMP-stimulated phosphodiesterase PDE2A in human venous and capillary endothelial cells (PMID: 10375378)
biological.summary: PDE2A is expressed in venous and capillary endothelial cells in cardiac and renal tissue but not in arterial endothelial cells. PDE2A is detected in endothelial cells of microvessels in renal glomerulus, skin, brain, and liver, suggesting a role in modulating cyclic nucleotide effects on fluid and inflammatory cell transit through the endothelial barrier.

biological.citation: PDE2A Inhibition Enhances Axonal Sprouting, Functional Connectivity, and Recovery after Stroke (PMID: 36163142)
biological.summary: PDE2A inhibition enhances motor recovery, increases axonal projections in peri-infarct cortex, and enhances functional connectivity of motor system excitatory neurons in a mouse cortical stroke model. PDE2A is enriched in cortex and its inhibition activates CREB-dependent neuronal growth responses without affecting angiogenesis, gliogenesis, neurogenesis, or inflammatory responses.
biological.sample_size: Young adult and aged male mice

biological.citation: Defects in AMPAR trafficking and microglia activation underlie socio-cognitive deficits associated to decreased expression of phosphodiesterase 2 a (PMID: 38154608)
biological.summary: Pde2a+/- heterozygous mice display sex-dependent socio-cognitive deficits with males showing severe phenotypes throughout life. PDE2A haploinsufficiency causes microglia activation, elevated glutathione levels, and increased GluR1 externalization in CA1, producing reduced mGluR-dependent long-term depression. PDE2A translation is negatively modulated by FMRP in Fragile X Syndrome models.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Biallelic founder mutation in PDE2A causes paroxysmal dyskinesia with Intellectual disability in Pakistani families
biological.summary: A homozygous missense variant c.1490T>C (p.Phe497Ser) in PDE2A was identified as a founder mutation in three unrelated Pakistani families with intellectual developmental disorder, paroxysmal dyskinesia, and seizures. PDE2A is critical for temporal regulation of cAMP and cGMP, modulating neuronal function, proliferation, apoptosis, and differentiation.
biological.sample_size: Six affected individuals across three families
